# Xu Programming Language

> Xu is a systems language with custom native AOT backends, zero GC, inferred ownership, and Go-like concurrency.

Official website: https://xulang.org
Language repository: https://github.com/xulang-org/xu
Selected released SDK: 0.10.7
License: MIT (see the repository LICENSE; preserve third-party notices).

## Language and safety model

Xu uses static typing, ownership inference, borrow checking, and deterministic resource cleanup. It uses custom AOT backends rather than LLVM. Coroutines start with `xu f()` and communicate through typed channels. There is no garbage collector.

Ownership and borrow diagnostics constrain value use and mutable access. Shared mutable state in concurrent code still requires appropriate synchronization. Native code, FFI, and concurrent libraries have their own safety requirements; this is not a blanket guarantee against every data race or undefined behavior. See https://xulang.org/docs/lang/memory/ and https://xulang.org/docs/lang/concurrency/.

Parameters, fields, and receivers use `name Type`, without a colon. Bindings use `name := value`, with a `$` prefix (`$name := value`) for reassignment; `$&T` is an exclusive borrow. `<<` returns, `>>` throws, and `or (err) { ... }` handles errors. Error text is obtained with `err.msg()`.

## Complete examples

Save each block in its own `main.xu`, then run `xu check main.xu` and `xu run main.xu`. These examples share their sources with the site playground and the bundled official error-handling example.

### Hello world

```xu
@main

fn main() int {
    println("Hello from XU Programming Language!")
    << 0
}
```

### Coroutines and channels

Use `chan int{cap: N}`, `ch <- value` to send, and `<-ch` to receive. The example collects three results before exiting.

```xu
@main

fn worker(id int, results chan int) {
    results <- id * 10
}

fn main() int {
    results := chan int{cap: 3}
    xu worker(1, results)
    xu worker(2, results)
    xu worker(3, results)

    $total := 0
    for i in 0:3 {
        value := <-results
        total += value
    }
    println(total)
    << 0
}
```

### Error handling

```xu
@main

#errors

fn read_name(ok bool) string {
    if !ok {
        >> errors.new("empty name")
    }
    << "ada"
}

fn load_or_fallback(ok bool) string {
    << read_name(ok) or (err) {
        println(err.msg())
        << "fallback"
    }
}

fn main() int {
    s := load_or_fallback(false)
    println(s)

    t := read_name(true) or (err) {
        println(err.msg())
        << 1
    }
    println(t)
    << 0
}
```

## Tools and package installation

- `xu build main.xu -o app`: compile a native executable.
- `xu run main.xu`: compile and execute.
- `xu check main.xu`: check syntax, types, and ownership.
- `xu debug main.xu`: build with debug information and launch LLDB, with GDB as fallback; an installed debugger is required.
- `xu test test.example.xu -v`: execute tests. Test and benchmark functions belong in `test.<name>.xu`, in `@main`, without parameters or return types.
- `xu fmt main.xu`: format source.
- `xu lsp`: serve LSP over stdin/stdout. Completion mainly covers keywords, built-ins, and current-file declarations. References use identifier text matching in the current file and same-directory Xu files; rename edits only the current file. Review edits for unrelated identifiers with the same spelling.
- `xu install`: resolve dependencies already declared in `xu.xun`, populate `vendor/`, and write `xu.lock`.
- `xu get <module>@<version>`: syntax template for adding a dependency with a verified published SemVer tag. Replace both placeholders. A module's declared version does not establish that a matching Git tag exists.
- `xu native`: compile/archive native modules, pack `.xulib` slices, and inspect/extract them. One-step static linking with `xu build`/`xu run` currently supports `macos-arm64` and `macos-x64` only. Other targets require object emission, conversion, and external linking.

Use the official packages bundled with the selected SDK, or the matching immutable source commit documented at https://xulang.org/docs/packages/. External imports use an explicit alias and full module path, for example `redis #github.com/xulang-org/packages/redis`. Standard-library and local-package imports have separate resolution rules (`#fmt`, `#util`). Redis connections use `redis.open`, `open_auth`, or `open_url`; consult the API for exact signatures. SQLite requires a prepared native bridge and the target's native toolchain.

## SDK, playground, and development scope

The browser playground implements a language subset with cooperative channel scheduling. Real multithreading, networking, C FFI, and desktop UI require the native SDK. See https://xulang.org/playground/ for the current sandbox limits.

XACP documentation describes the language repository's development branch after PR #23, separately from the selected released SDK. The implementation includes stdio and loopback TCP control. See https://xulang.org/api/xacp/ and https://github.com/xulang-org/xu/blob/dev/examples/xacp/README.md. `xu xacp debug` inspects and launches a program; source debugging uses `xu debug`.

## Benchmark evidence

The published dashboard contains 47 workloads across 6 platforms, measured with Xu 0.10.7 on 2026-10-26. The measurement identity is independent of the selected SDK. See https://xulang.org/benchmarks/ and the source CI run: https://github.com/xulang-org/bench/actions/runs/40298620461. Consult the dashboard's per-platform results and methodology rather than infer a universal speedup.

## Additional syntax examples

Each block is a complete independent program from the site's playground examples or ownership tutorial. Save one at a time as `main.xu`.

### Bindings and mutability

```xu
@main

const MAX = 100

fn main() int {
    name := "Xu"
    $age := 20
    age += 1
    println(name)
    println(age)
    println(MAX)
    << 0
}
```

### Structs and methods

```xu
@main

struct Counter {
    n int
}

fn (c Counter) get() int {
    << c.n
}

fn (c $&Counter) inc() {
    c.n += 1
}

fn main() int {
    $counter := Counter{n: 10}
    println(counter.get())
    counter.inc()
    println(counter.get())
    << 0
}
```

### Borrowing

`&T` denotes a shared borrow; `$&T` denotes an exclusive mutable borrow. Follow compiler diagnostics for inferred ownership and borrow lifetimes.

```xu
@main

fn take(s string) {
    println(s)
}

fn len_of(s &string) int {
    << s.len
}

fn append_bang(s $&string) {
    s.push_str("!")
}

fn main() int {
    msg := "hello"
    println(len_of(&msg))
    println(msg)

    $owned := "hi"
    append_bang($&owned)
    println(owned)

    take(owned)
    // owned 已 move，不可再使用
    << 0
}
```

### Loops and control flow

`<-` breaks a loop and `->` continues it. `<<` returns from a function; `<<<` exits the process.

```xu
@main

fn main() int {
    for i in 0:10 {
        if i >= 7 { <- }
        if i % 2 == 0 { -> }
        println(i)
    }
    << 0
}
```

## Project manifest and dependency workflow

Place the project beside the extracted SDK directory named `xu-v0.10.7`, or adjust the local path below to the installed SDK's packages directory:

```xun
module: myapp
version: !ver 0.1.0
xu: !ver 0.10.7
require:
  "github.com/xulang-org/packages": file:../xu-v0.10.7/packages
```

From the project root, run:

```sh
xu install
xu check main.xu --offline
xu build main.xu --frozen -o app
```

Commit the application manifest and lockfile for reproducibility. For fetching the SDK's exact source commit instead of using a local bundle, follow https://xulang.org/docs/packages/. Native bridge artifacts may require separate preparation; installing Xu source dependencies does not build those artifacts.

## Tests

Save this as `test.example.xu`:

```xu
@main

fn test_add() {
    assert(1 + 1 == 2)
}
```

Run `xu test test.example.xu -v`. Benchmark functions follow the same filename and signature restrictions, use the `bench_` prefix, and are selected with `-bench REGEXP`.

## Native container metadata

The product `xu native pack` writes top-level `abi`, `format`, `module`, and `slices` metadata. Export signatures are stored in each slice's XUOBJ metadata. The source-tree Python helper `scripts/xunative.py` also retains fields copied from its input manifest, including `exports`; consumers must not assume every product-generated container has top-level `exports`.

Packing multiple target slices and linking a native executable are separate capabilities. The one-step macOS link path needs the macOS C toolchain. For other targets, emit XUOBJ with `--emit-obj`, convert to a platform object, and use the target's external linker. See https://xulang.org/docs/native/ for platform scope.

## Standard library and integrations

The API catalog at https://xulang.org/api/ is generated from the selected released SDK. It covers formatting, errors, collections, text and encodings, files and processes, networking, cryptography, SQL, and the `ui`, `ui/draw`, `ui/layout`, `ui/widgets`, and `ui/webview` packages. Consult each package's documented target limits.

Official service integrations live in the independent https://github.com/xulang-org/packages repository. The website documents the SDK's pinned package snapshot, which can differ from that repository's current branch. Read the relevant API and example before assuming a protocol feature or native target is supported.
